Cherry eye surgery for bulldogs

What is cherry eye?

Cherry eye is a prolapse of the third eyelid gland and it is common in English and French bulldogs. Surgery repositions the gland instead of removing it, because that gland produces a large share of the tear film and taking it out leads to dry eye later in the dog's life.

How long is recovery?

Recovery takes ten to fourteen days with a soft collar. Recurrence happens in roughly ten per cent of dogs and a second procedure is usually successful.
